candidates.title: Enterprise concurrent share sync loses acknowledged updates
candidates.trigger: Two sync requests for the same share read the same snapshot before either writes
candidates.consequence: Both succeed but the final snapshot retains only one request
candidates.decisive_evidence: /tmp/graphagent-services-share-probe.ts imports actual Share, uses isolated memory Storage. Submitted distinct message IDs a,b concurrently; result retained only b.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Serialize mutations per share in the deployed ownership boundary, or use storage atomic conditional writes with retry; ensure multi-process safety rather than a process-local lock alone.
candidates.acceptance: Concurrent non-overlapping sync updates both retained; races with remove/create cannot resurrect stale snapshots.

candidates.title: Enterprise simultaneous share creation returns competing secrets
candidates.trigger: Two create requests derive the same share ID and both finish get before writes
candidates.consequence: Both callers receive success with distinct secrets; only the last secret authorizes subsequent sync
candidates.decisive_evidence: /tmp/graphagent-services-share-probe.ts: bothSucceeded=true, differentSecrets=true, acceptedSecrets=[false,true]. No credentials printed.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Atomic create-if-absent under the deployed shared storage ownership model.
candidates.acceptance: Exactly one success and one AlreadyExists, winner remains authoritative.

candidates.title: Enterprise storage list ignores continuation pages
candidates.trigger: Share prefix exceeds the object-store ListObjectsV2 first page
candidates.consequence: Remove leaves legacy data objects; legacy reconstruction omits later objects
candidates.decisive_evidence: Decisive source counterexample: XML IsTruncated/NextContinuationToken is never read; one HTTP GET, one Key scan, then return. No network reproduction performed.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Follow continuation-token while respecting explicit total limit; correctly decode XML keys.
candidates.acceptance: Simulated two-page response returns all keys; remove deletes objects beyond first page; limit/before/after semantics retained.

candidates.title: Enterprise share data cache outlives revocation
candidates.trigger: A shared cache stores GET data before owner deletes share
candidates.consequence: Cache can serve conversation after deletion for 300s freshness and stale revalidation policy up to 86400s
candidates.decisive_evidence: Response explicitly public max-age=30,s-maxage=300,stale-while-revalidate=86400; deletion neither purges shared caches nor changes URL. Source decisive; deployed cache not accessed.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use no-store for revocable share data or integrate verified cache invalidation with successful revocation.
candidates.acceptance: GET policy cannot reuse revoked conversation; isolated cache integration asserts DELETE prevents later cached data access.

candidates.title: Provider list sends raw workspace credentials to browser
candidates.trigger: A workspace member invokes the exported provider.list server query
candidates.consequence: Full provider credentials cross server boundary despite UI masking and admin-only mutation
candidates.decisive_evidence: Provider.list selects all columns with only workspace/deletion conditions; getActor permits members; listProviders returns result directly; masking occurs client-side. No real DB accessed.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Return public provider metadata and a server-computed masked display; keep secret lookup internal to inference.
candidates.acceptance: Admin/member query wire output never contains raw fixture secret; provider execution still uses server-side credential.

candidates.title: SQLite preparation errors escape typed SqlError channel
candidates.trigger: Malformed SQL or a query references a nonexistent table
candidates.consequence: Normal database error becomes Effect defect, bypassing catchTag SqlError
candidates.decisive_evidence: /tmp/graphagent-services-sqlite-probe.ts executes actual client in :memory:, SELECT nonexistent_table -> Exit Failure reason Die. No user DB accessed.
candidates.why_not_design: Observable behavior contradicts the implemented ownership, cumulative-data, revocation or typed-error contract.
candidates.suggested_fix: Move prepare/configuration into try catch for both run and runValues; retain classifier and interruption behavior.
candidates.acceptance: Missing table and invalid syntax fail with SqlError rather than Die for both row modes; valid queries/transactions unaffected.

candidates.title: Removed workspace member retains usable inference API key
candidates.trigger: Admin removes a member while their key is active
candidates.consequence: Old key still authenticates and charges workspace balance
candidates.decisive_evidence: User.remove only updates UserTable.timeDeleted. Authenticate joins user/workspace but filters only active KeyTable. Account.remove separately revokes keys, providing existing intended removal pattern.
candidates.why_not_design: Contradicts member revocation, caller credential confidentiality or local-daemon API scope.
candidates.suggested_fix: Revoke member keys transactionally and require active user/workspace in inference authentication.
candidates.acceptance: Synthetic removed user and deleted workspace cannot authenticate, active members remain accepted.

candidates.title: Zen proxy forwards caller credentials to third-party providers
candidates.trigger: Caller uses Zen Authorization bearer and selects standard Anthropic or Google provider
candidates.consequence: Zen key and other incoming sensitive headers remain in upstream request
candidates.decisive_evidence: new Headers(input.request.headers) followed by ordinary Anthropic setting only x-api-key (Google only x-goog-api-key); original Authorization/Cookie not removed. Bedrock/OpenAI overwrite Authorization, so those are excluded from the claim.
candidates.why_not_design: Contradicts member revocation, caller credential confidentiality or local-daemon API scope.
candidates.suggested_fix: Allowlist protocol headers from caller, then add upstream provider credentials; never forward caller Authorization/Cookie.
candidates.acceptance: Mock upstream asserts caller secret absent while provider key and required Anthropic/Google headers retained.

candidates.title: CLI API path can redirect authenticated request to another origin
candidates.trigger: User passes raw API path //fixture.invalid/api or equivalent slash/backslash URL
candidates.consequence: Daemon Basic credential headers are sent to resolved external origin
candidates.decisive_evidence: Isolated WHATWG URL counterexample accepts startsWith slash but new URL yields http://fixture.invalid; no network performed. Trigger requires supplied CLI argument, not remote unauthenticated execution.
candidates.why_not_design: Contradicts member revocation, caller credential confidentiality or local-daemon API scope.
candidates.suggested_fix: Validate final resolved URL origin equals daemon origin; reject protocol-relative and normalized slash/backslash escape forms.
candidates.acceptance: Mock fetch must never execute foreign-origin request; valid local paths and operation/query resolution preserved.
